name: American Airports
description:
American Airports Corporation, under contract with the County of Los Angeles, is responsible for the management and operation of this uncontrolled 77-acre general aviation airport. The airport is located near Interstate 91 and the new Home Depot Center sports complex, about 10 miles south of downtown Los Angeles.

Compton / Woodley Airport has 275 based aircraft and experiences over 66,000 annual operations off of its two paved parallel runways: 7L/25R and 7R/25L. Runway 7L/25R is 3,670 feet long and 60 feet wide, with no lighting. It is used for VFR operations during the day only. Runway 7R/25L is 3,670 feet long and 60 feet wide, with medium intensity runway lighting (MIRL). It has runway end identifier lights and a two box precision approach path indicator (PAPI).

Quality AvFuel 100LL Avgas is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You can fuel your aircraft yourself at the self-serve pumps, or you can call for the fuel truck to come service your plane.

Several aviation-related businesses are located at Compton. They perform such functions as aircraft maintenance and painting, pilot supply sales, flight training and banner towing. There is also a museum located at the airport that helps mentor tomorrow’s pilots.

At Inflight, our clients always come first. Our team is made up of pilots who share a safety-first mindset and a deep understanding of what matters most to those who fly.

We look forward to welcoming you to Inflight Aviation and redefining your expectations of what an FBO can be.

Trever Rossini

description:
The Natchitoches Regional Airport (KIER) is located at 450 Wallenberg Drive, just southwest of downtown Natchitoches, Louisiana. Natchitoches Regional Airport sits at an elevation of 121 feet, and offers two runways.  Runway 17/35 measures 5,000 x 150 feet, which is critical to landing larger corporate jets, and is lighted and paved. Runway 7/25 is 4,000 x 100 feet, and is also lighted and paved. The main ramp, fuel pumps, and terminal are midfield, east of Runway 17/35, which is the runway most commonly used.

Tiedowns are free, and hangar space may be available (please call ahead for availability). The Airport provides a full-service mechanic shop that is on call 24 hours a day. Rental cars are available through Enterprise and Hertz, as well as two courtesy cars which may be available.

The main terminal has a shower, kitchenette, wireless Internet, DSL, and a pilot lounge with computerized weather. 100LL and Jet fuel are available from automated fuel pumps 24 hours a day, with full service or assisted service fueling by an on-site attendant during daylight hours.  The airport has a 2,200 gallon Jet-A fuel truck which can fuel aircraft quickly and conveniently, single point, or over the wing. The terminal is staffed dawn to dusk, with 24-hour call out.

Now open!

Centrally located between Honolulu and Ko Olina, the John Rodgers Airport (PHJR) in Kalaeloa, Hawaii is the ideal gateway to your recreational or professional trip in this tropical paradise. The airport’s location, infrastructure, and low air traffic compared to Honolulu International Airport (HNL), make PHJR the optimal choice for aircraft traveling to and from the United States Mainland. Planned development and additional upgrades make PHJR an excellent alternative to HNL, and a valuable asset to business and tourism within the Hawaiian islands.

No matter how you fly, you’ll find the Ultimate VIP Experience – along with the concierge amenities and outstanding customer service that you have come to expect from the Million Air brand – at Million Air Honolulu.

“As an organization, we are always looking for underutilized airports across the country that would benefit from our involvement and private investment that would serve as a catalyst for increasing activity as these types of airports. We have had a successful track record of accomplishing these goals at other airports where we currently operate. – Scott Freeman, CEO

hours: 7:30 am to 5:30 pm daily; after on req
description:
The Bryce Canyon Airport is located just four miles north of Bryce Canyon National Park, making it the perfect gateway access to all of scenic Bryce Canyon Country.
The Bryce Canyon Airport is located just four miles north of Bryce Canyon National Park, making it the perfect gateway access to all of scenic Bryce Canyon Country.

The asphalt-paved, single-runway airport accommodates hundreds of flights each year. The airport is at an elevation of 7,586 feet, and flights from here offer a birds-eye view of some of Bryce Canyon Country’s most spectacular scenery.

Bryce Canyon Helicopters is the main operator out of Bryce Canyon Airport, offering helicopter rides over Bryce Canyon National Park, the Grand Canyon, Lake Powell, Grand Staircase Escalante National Monument, Zion National Park, and more. Small airlines from Arizona and Nevada also frequent Bryce Canyon Airport.

The Bryce Canyon Airport was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978, and its original log hangar from its days as the Garfield County Airport still stands. Built from local ponderosa pine in 1936 by the Works Progress Administration, a New Deal program that employed unskilled workers, the log hangar used traditional construction techniques in stark contrast to the new aviation technology it would soon house. “If you build it they will come,” and so the Bryce Canyon Airport has encouraged and enhanced tourism for the past 75 years.

Although the Bryce Canyon Airport typically handles small aircraft, the 7,400-foot long, 75-foot wide runway was designed to accommodate larger aircraft on demand. This fortunate foresight saved the lives of 75 passengers and crew aboard American Airlines flight 2821 on October 6, 2000, when the Los Angeles-bound MD-82 from Denver lost cabin pressure at 33,000 feet and landed safely at Bryce Canyon Airport.

name: City of Natchitoches Regional Airport
hours: daylight; 24 on req
description:
The Natchitoches Regional Airport (KIER) is located at 450 Wallenberg Drive, just southwest of downtown Natchitoches, Louisiana. Natchitoches Regional Airport sits at an elevation of 121 feet, and offers two runways.  Runway 17/35 measures 5,000 x 150 feet, which is critical to landing larger corporate jets, and is lighted and paved. Runway 7/25 is 4,000 x 100 feet, and is also lighted and paved. The main ramp, fuel pumps, and terminal are midfield, east of Runway 17/35, which is the runway most commonly used.

Tiedowns are free, and hangar space may be available (please call ahead for availability). The Airport provides a full-service mechanic shop that is on call 24 hours a day. Rental cars are available through Enterprise and Hertz, as well as two courtesy cars which may be available.

The main terminal has a shower, kitchenette, wireless Internet, DSL, and a pilot lounge with computerized weather. 100LL and Jet fuel are available from automated fuel pumps 24 hours a day, with full service or assisted service fueling by an on-site attendant during daylight hours.  The airport has a 2,200 gallon Jet-A fuel truck which can fuel aircraft quickly and conveniently, single point, or over the wing. The terminal is staffed dawn to dusk, with 24-hour call out.

hours: 6 am to 10 pm
description:
About Us
Located in the southeastern part of Mineral Wells, Texas, the airport was built by the U. S. Army and opened in 1943 to support the nearby infantry training facility, Camp Wolters. Camp Wolters grew to become an important infantry replacement training center, housing more than 24,000 soldiers at its peak. The camp was closed after the war ended.

In early 1951, the U. S. Air Force reopened the camp and renamed it Wolters Air Force Base. The base was used to train special army and air force personnel and the airport provided support.

In September of 1956, the U. S. Army regained control of the base and gave it a new name, the Primary Helicopter Center. It was primarily used to train helicopter pilots.

In June 1963, the base was again renamed, this time to be called Fort Wolters. At that time, all army helicopter pilots' basic and primary flight training was provided there. The Vietnam War expanded its role to include the training of Marine Corps and Air Force pilots.

The airport served in a support role through all of the changes, adding the Downing Hangar, two other buildings, and over 54 acres of tarmac in 1966 to expand helicopter pilot training during the Vietnam War.

There are more than 50 T-hangars and 10 box hangars on the airport, and more are planned each year to support the rapid westward growth of the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex.

description:
The story of the St. Clair County Airport began in 1966 when a parcel of land was purchased from Marlin Hugghins and designated an airport property. The runway, taxiway and airport grounds and facilities were completed the same year, and the opening was attended by then-Governor George Wallace. Over the years the airport has been home to several military reserve units, an EAA chapter and a Civil Air Patrol unit.

While it will always be a general aviation airport, the FAA has designated KPLR as a “reliever” airport for Birmingham. Even with its elevation to reliever status, the airport still supports a vibrant general and corporate aviation community. Current amenities include multiple sizes of hangars available for rent, a flight training school, aviation maintenance facilities and an avionics shop. With a new FBO and 24-hour AVGAS availability, improvements at the airport continue as implementation of its FAA Master Plan progresses.

description:
American Airports Corporation, under contract with the County of Los Angeles, is responsible for the management and operation of this controlled 276-acre general aviation airport. The Airport is located within the city limits of La Verne, 25 miles east of downtown Los Angeles, right next door to the L.A. County Fairplex, Pomona Raceway and Raging Waters theme park.

Brackett has 482 based aircraft and experiences over 115,600 annual operations. The airport has two paved runways. Runway 8R/26L, the primary runway, is 4,839 feet long, 75 feet wide, with medium intensity runway lighting (MIRL). The secondary runway, runway 8L/26R, is 3,661 feet long and 75 feet wide. The Airport has one precision approach (ILS RW 26L), and each end of runway 8R/26L is equipped with precision approach path indicators (PAPI). Brackett is also home to a state-of-the-art FAA air traffic control tower. The POM VOR is just 1 mile south.

Brackett has over 400 rental hangars and over 100 rental tie downs. Please check our Available Properties page for more information regarding Brackett’s current space availabilities and rates.

Quality AvFuel Jet A and 100LL Avgas are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You can fuel your aircraft yourself at the self-serve pumps, or you can call for the fuel truck to come service your plane. Aeroshell aviation oil and Deice jet fuel additive are also available.

Several businesses call Brackett Field Airport “home”. They perform such functions as helicopter maintenance, aircraft maintenance, instrument sales and repairs, and aircraft interior sales. The Mount San Antonio College Aviation Department also bases its A&P and flight schools at Brackett.

description:
~ABOUT THE FBO~

Golden State Aviation is a relatively small full service FBO. We cater to the needs of small to medium corporate jets. we are not the big fancy plush FBO but we will take great care of you and your customers. We offer overnight, short and long term parking at our location. Shell Aviation Certified Dealer. Serving Aviation since 1968. No Ramp Fee and Free outside Parking w/purchase. Free courtesy/crew car w/purchase of Jet A when available Start Cart no charge. 24 Hr callouts $100: Call Mike Roberts 24/7 at 619-368-0065. We look forward to serving you.

~ABOUT THE CLUB~

Its easy to join the club. You and your family and relatives can join for only $26 per month per family. Dues are payable by the month, no minimum number of months required. 

Your membership entitles you to free use of the club facilities, headsets, flight simulator, WiFi, computer, printer, coffee, etc. 

Members can use the club aircraft on trips and only pay for flight time... there is no daily minimum... and all the fuel you use is paid for by the club. Insurance is included in the rates and has a deductible of only $100. 

For example you can take a plane to Palm Springs for a three day weekend and only pay for the hour over and back. This three day trip to Palm Springs would cost $200 round trip for four, so only $50 each including all fuel and insurance!!! Cheaper than renting a car. 

When you join you will pay $550 in prepaid flying to establish your membership. This $550 is returned to you when you resign the club. 

When you fly you do not pay at the time of the flight, you just sign for the flight and we will bill you at the end of the month. You then have until the 10th of the following month to pay. 

We accept all credit and debit cards, checks and cash. 

New student pilots are welcome, as well as licensed pilots.

name: Somerset-Pulaski County Airport
description:
About the Airport
Lake Cumberland Regional Airport (IATA: SME, ICAO: KSME, FAA LID: SME) is a public use airport located three nautical miles (6 km) south of the central business district of Somerset, a city in Pulaski County, Kentucky, United States. The airport is owned by the city of Somerset and Pulaski County. It also serves the area around Lake Cumberland. It is mostly used for general aviation, and from late 2008 until February 2010, was served by one commercial airline, Locair. The $3 million federally funded passenger terminal was converted to the FBO in September 2011. The airport was renamed in 2008; it was formerly known as Somerset-Pulaski County Airport or J.T. Wilson Field.

Lake Cumberland Regional Airport covers an area of 288 acres (117 ha) at an elevation of 927 feet (283 m) above mean sea level. It has one asphalt paved runway designated 05/23 which measures 5,801 by 100 feet (1,768 x 30 m). For the 12-month period ending August 31, 2008, the airport had 27,605 aircraft operations, an average of 75 per day: 99% general aviation and 1% military. At that time there were 28 aircraft based at this airport: 71% single-engine, 14% multi-engine, 4% jet and 11% helicopter.

WX AWOS-3: 120.050 (606-679-5710)

description:
American Airports Corporation, under contract with the County of Los Angeles, is responsible for the management and operation of this controlled 184-acre general aviation airport, which is located in the middle of the San Fernando Valley between three major freeways (the I-5, 210 and 118), with downtown Los Angeles 15 miles to the southeast and Santa Monica 15 miles to the south.

Whiteman Airport has 600 based aircraft and experiences over 115,000 annual operations. The airport is home to a state-of-the-art contract air traffic control tower and multiple aviation-related businesses, including three major maintenance repair stations, multiple flight schools and helicopter maintenance operations. The airport is often a backdrop for the motion picture industry, with several major motion pictures having been filmed there.

Whiteman Airport has one paved runway. Runway 12/30 is 4,120 feet long and 75 feet wide, and is equipped with medium intensity runway lighting (MIRL). Each end of the runway is equipped with a two-light precision approach path indicator lighting (PAPI).

Quality AvFuel Jet A and 100LL Avgas are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You can fuel your aircraft yourself at the self-serve pumps, or you can call for the fuel truck to come service your plane.

The airport is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year. Fuel and oil can be purchased at any time. Fuel services can be reached by calling (818) 312-2911 or by using the Unicom frequency – 122.95.

General WIlliam J. Fox Airfield (WJF)
Located in the heart of California's Antelope Valley, WJF serves as a key general aviation facility for the Lancaster and greater Los Angeles County region. 

Fox Field is a popular base for both recreational and business aviation, with on-site services including fuel, maintenance, hangars, and flight training.  The airport also supports Cal Fire and USFS air operations during fire season and offers easy access to the Mojave Desert, Edwards Air Force Base, and aerospace industry hubs.

Foxy's Landing & Restaurant is located inside the terminal building.  This cozy eatery serves breakfast and lunch, allowing patrons to enjoy meals while watching aircraft activity on the runway.  Operating hours are typically from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM.  For the most current hours or to make inquiries, it's advisable to contact the restaurant directly at (661) 949-2284.

With its towered airspace and welcoming pilot amenities, WJF is a dependable stop for transient traffic and a valuable resource for the local aviation community.

hours: 6 am to 10 pm
description:
About Us
Located in the southeastern part of Mineral Wells, Texas, the airport was built by the U. S. Army and opened in 1943 to support the nearby infantry training facility, Camp Wolters. Camp Wolters grew to become an important infantry replacement training center, housing more than 24,000 soldiers at its peak. The camp was closed after the war ended.

In early 1951, the U. S. Air Force reopened the camp and renamed it Wolters Air Force Base. The base was used to train special army and air force personnel and the airport provided support.

In September of 1956, the U. S. Army regained control of the base and gave it a new name, the Primary Helicopter Center. It was primarily used to train helicopter pilots.

In June 1963, the base was again renamed, this time to be called Fort Wolters. At that time, all army helicopter pilots' basic and primary flight training was provided there. The Vietnam War expanded its role to include the training of Marine Corps and Air Force pilots.

The airport served in a support role through all of the changes, adding the Downing Hangar, two other buildings, and over 54 acres of tarmac in 1966 to expand helicopter pilot training during the Vietnam War.

There are more than 50 T-hangars and 10 box hangars on the airport, and more are planned each year to support the rapid westward growth of the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex.

description:
Now open!

Centrally located between Honolulu and Ko Olina, the John Rodgers Airport (PHJR) in Kalaeloa, Hawaii is the ideal gateway to your recreational or professional trip in this tropical paradise. The airport’s location, infrastructure, and low air traffic compared to Honolulu International Airport (HNL), make PHJR the optimal choice for aircraft traveling to and from the United States Mainland. John Rodgers Field can accommodate a wide variety of aircraft with its expansive ramps and long runways – 8,000 ft. and 6,000 ft. The airfield has recently undergone significant improvements including partial runway resurfacing, airfield lighting, communications and emergency systems. Planned development and additional upgrades make PHJR an excellent alternative to HNL, and a valuable asset to business and tourism within the Hawaiian islands.

Million Air Honolulu aims to boost aviation traffic in Kapolei with the addition of a planned 30,000 sq. ft. hangar, 8,000 sq. ft. state-of-the-art FBO and café, and a brand new fuel farm – planned capacity of 240,000 gallons of Jet Fuel and 15,000 gallons of AvGas. No matter how you fly, you’ll find the Ultimate VIP Experience – along with the concierge amenities and outstanding customer service that you have come to expect from the Million Air brand – at Million Air Honolulu.

“As an organization, we are always looking for underutilized airports across the country that would benefit from our involvement and private investment that would serve as a catalyst for increasing activity as these types of airports. We have had a successful track record of accomplishing these goals at other airports where we currently operate. We have long had (Kalaeloa) on our list of potential growth locations, and after some due diligence, we felt it was a project worth pursuing.” 

– Scott Freeman, CEO

address: St Clair County Airport, 240 Airport Road
hours: 7 am to dark; after on req 205/369-2771
description:
The story of the St. Clair County Airport began in 1966 when a parcel of land was purchased from Marlin Hugghins and designated an airport property. The runway, taxiway and airport grounds and facilities were completed the same year, and the opening was attended by then-Governor George Wallace. Over the years the airport has been home to several military reserve units, an EAA chapter and a Civil Air Patrol unit.

While it will always be a general aviation airport, the FAA has designated KPLR as a “reliever” airport for Birmingham. Even with its elevation to reliever status, the airport still supports a vibrant general and corporate aviation community. Current amenities include multiple sizes of hangars available for rent, a flight training school, aviation maintenance facilities and an avionics shop. With a new FBO and 24-hour AVGAS availability, improvements at the airport continue as implementation of its FAA Master Plan progresses.

description:
American Airports Corporation, under contract with the County of Los Angeles, is responsible for the management and operation of this controlled 276-acre general aviation airport. The Airport is located within the city limits of La Verne, 25 miles east of downtown Los Angeles, right next door to the L.A. County Fairplex, Pomona Raceway and Raging Waters theme park.

Brackett has 482 based aircraft and experiences over 115,600 annual operations. The airport has two paved runways. Runway 8R/26L, the primary runway, is 4,839 feet long, 75 feet wide, with medium intensity runway lighting (MIRL). The secondary runway, runway 8L/26R, is 3,661 feet long and 75 feet wide. The Airport has one precision approach (ILS RW 26L), and each end of runway 8R/26L is equipped with precision approach path indicators (PAPI). Brackett is also home to a state-of-the-art FAA air traffic control tower. The POM VOR is just 1 mile south.

Brackett has over 400 rental hangars and over 100 rental tie downs. Please check our Available Properties page for more information regarding Brackett’s current space availabilities and rates.

Quality AvFuel Jet A and 100LL Avgas are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You can fuel your aircraft yourself at the self-serve pumps, or you can call for the fuel truck to come service your plane. Aeroshell aviation oil and Deice jet fuel additive are also available.

Several businesses call Brackett Field Airport “home”. They perform such functions as helicopter maintenance, aircraft maintenance, instrument sales and repairs, and aircraft interior sales. The Mount San Antonio College Aviation Department also bases its A&P and flight schools at Brackett.

description:
~ABOUT THE FBO~

Golden State Aviation is a relatively small full service FBO. We cater to the needs of small to medium corporate jets. we are not the big fancy plush FBO but we will take great care of you and your customers. We offer overnight, short and long term parking at our location. Shell Aviation Certified Dealer. Serving Aviation since 1968. No Ramp Fee and Free outside Parking w/purchase. Free courtesy/crew car w/purchase of Jet A when available Start Cart no charge. 24 Hr callouts $100: Call Mike Roberts 24/7 at 619-368-0065. We look forward to serving you.

~ABOUT THE CLUB~

Its easy to join the club. You and your family and relatives can join for only $26 per month per family. Dues are payable by the month, no minimum number of months required. 

Your membership entitles you to free use of the club facilities, headsets, flight simulator, WiFi, computer, printer, coffee, etc. 

Members can use the club aircraft on trips and only pay for flight time... there is no daily minimum... and all the fuel you use is paid for by the club. Insurance is included in the rates and has a deductible of only $100. 

For example you can take a plane to Palm Springs for a three day weekend and only pay for the hour over and back. This three day trip to Palm Springs would cost $200 round trip for four, so only $50 each including all fuel and insurance!!! Cheaper than renting a car. 

When you join you will pay $550 in prepaid flying to establish your membership. This $550 is returned to you when you resign the club. 

When you fly you do not pay at the time of the flight, you just sign for the flight and we will bill you at the end of the month. You then have until the 10th of the following month to pay. 

We accept all credit and debit cards, checks and cash. 

New student pilots are welcome, as well as licensed pilots.

name: Somerset-Pulaski County Airport
description:
About the Airport
Lake Cumberland Regional Airport (IATA: SME, ICAO: KSME, FAA LID: SME) is a public use airport located three nautical miles (6 km) south of the central business district of Somerset, a city in Pulaski County, Kentucky, United States. The airport is owned by the city of Somerset and Pulaski County. It also serves the area around Lake Cumberland. It is mostly used for general aviation, and from late 2008 until February 2010, was served by one commercial airline, Locair. The $3 million federally funded passenger terminal was converted to the FBO in September 2011. The airport was renamed in 2008; it was formerly known as Somerset-Pulaski County Airport or J.T. Wilson Field.

Lake Cumberland Regional Airport covers an area of 288 acres (117 ha) at an elevation of 927 feet (283 m) above mean sea level. It has one asphalt paved runway designated 05/23 which measures 5,801 by 100 feet (1,768 x 30 m). For the 12-month period ending August 31, 2008, the airport had 27,605 aircraft operations, an average of 75 per day: 99% general aviation and 1% military. At that time there were 28 aircraft based at this airport: 71% single-engine, 14% multi-engine, 4% jet and 11% helicopter.

Radio Frequencies
CTAF/UNICOM: 122.8
WX AWOS-3: 120.050 (606-679-5710)
WX AWOS-3PT at EKQ (17 nm SW): 118.825 (606-348-0862)
APCH/DEP SVC PRVDD BY INDIANAPOLIS ARTCC ON FREQS 124.625/371.925 (LONDON 2 RCAG).

name: American Airports Corp.
description:
American Airports Corporation, under contract with the County of Los Angeles, is responsible for the management and operation of this controlled 184-acre general aviation airport, which is located in the middle of the San Fernando Valley between three major freeways (the I-5, 210 and 118), with downtown Los Angeles 15 miles to the southeast and Santa Monica 15 miles to the south.

Whiteman Airport has 600 based aircraft and experiences over 115,000 annual operations. The airport is home to a state-of-the-art contract air traffic control tower and multiple aviation-related businesses, including three major maintenance repair stations, multiple flight schools and helicopter maintenance operations. The airport is often a backdrop for the motion picture industry, with several major motion pictures having been filmed there.

Whiteman Airport has one paved runway. Runway 12/30 is 4,120 feet long and 75 feet wide, and is equipped with medium intensity runway lighting (MIRL). Each end of the runway is equipped with a two-light precision approach path indicator lighting (PAPI).

Quality AvFuel Jet A and 100LL Avgas are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You can fuel your aircraft yourself at the self-serve pumps, or you can call for the fuel truck to come service your plane.

The airport is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year. Fuel and oil can be purchased at any time. Fuel services can be reached by calling (818) 312-2911 or by using the Unicom frequency – 122.95.

description:
To oversee the operation, maintenance, and development of the five County-owned general aviation airports (Brackett Field Airport, Compton/Woodley Airport, General Wm. J. Fox Airfield, and Gabriel Valley Airport, and Whiteman Airport).

General WIlliam J. Fox Airfield (WJF)
Located in the heart of California's Antelope Valley, WJF serves as a key general aviation facility for the Lancaster and greater Los Angeles County region. 

Fox Field is a popular base for both recreational and business aviation, with on-site services including fuel, maintenance, hangars, and flight training.  The airport also supports Cal Fire and USFS air operations during fire season and offers easy access to the Mojave Desert, Edwards Air Force Base, and aerospace industry hubs.

Foxy's Landing & Restaurant is located inside the terminal building.  This cozy eatery serves breakfast and lunch, allowing patrons to enjoy meals while watching aircraft activity on the runway.  Operating hours are typically from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM.  For the most current hours or to make inquiries, it's advisable to contact the restaurant directly at (661) 949-2284.

With its towered airspace and welcoming pilot amenities, WJF is a dependable stop for transient traffic and a valuable resource for the local aviation community.
